title: L'homme qui a attaqué une garderie suisse a trouvé ses victimes sur ChatGPT

reading.body:
This is a failure of a general-purpose language model being used outside its intended conditions to assist in planning a violent crime. The failure occurred at the point of user interaction, where the system answered queries about legal consequences of different murder methods and, according to one headline, helped locate victims, without refusing or flagging them. Catching it would have required the model to recognize and decline requests that facilitate serious violence, or a human review layer for such queries.

The failure mode is a model providing actionable information for a harmful plan without a human check. This is not a hallucination or an impersonation; it is a deployment gap where safety filters did not block clearly dangerous queries. The system was used as a research assistant for premeditated violence, far outside any legitimate purpose.

The prosecution's account is an allegation, not a judicial finding, and no evidence is provided that the AI provider intended or knowingly enabled the attack.

reports.title: Messerangriff auf Kinder: Täter «kaufte Rindfleisch, um zu üben»
Chinese hatte Tat zusammen mit ChatGPT geplant!
Zürich-Oerlikon: Angriff auf Kinder eines Kinderhortes mit Verletzungsfolgen
L'homme qui a attaqué une garderie suisse a trouvé ses victimes sur ChatGPT

summary:
A 23-year-old Chinese student attacked three five-year-old boys with a knife in Zurich-Oerlikon on October 1, 2024, causing severe injuries to all three children. One boy had his jugular vein completely severed and required emergency surgery to prevent death from blood loss, while another suffered stab wounds to the chest that damaged his heart sac and major blood vessels, also nearly fatal. A daycare worker stopped the attacker by restraining his arms, and passersby held him until police arrived. The prosecution describes the attack as extremely premeditated and cold-blooded, noting the man planned the violence using ChatGPT to research legal consequences of different murder methods.

The perpetrator, who came to Switzerland one year earlier to pursue a master's degree at the University of Zurich, carefully prepared for weeks. He purchased kitchen knives, researched where to find children, studied human anatomy and blood vessels, and bought raw beef in late September to practice knife techniques. He carried out the attack on the Chinese National Day, posting patriotic content on Instagram minutes beforehand. The prosecution charges him with attempted murder and is seeking 15 years imprisonment plus a 15-year ban from Switzerland, arguing he acted from revenge, vanity, and ideological delusion.
title_en: The man who attacked a Swiss daycare found his victims on ChatGPT
